title: Federated Launch Signal Translator + Cutover Fuse for Regional Release Trains
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Purpose: Define and deliver a lightweight Federated Launch Signal Translator (FLST) and an automated Cutover Fuse layer to reduce cross-team coordination friction during multi-region release trains (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments).

Scope:
- FLST: a small coordination service (stateless proxy + config) that ingests per-team launch signals (canary windows, capacity reservations, blackout periods) and emits harmonized launch windows plus translated human-readable constraints for console and runtime orchestration.
- Cutover Fuse: an enforcement/guardrail component that integrates with the deployment sequencer and runtime router to apply temporary safeholds (throttle, pause, fallback to older model variant) when regional capacity, SLO regressions, or incident signals are detected.

Goals:
1) Reduce manual cross-team gating steps for coordinated launches by ~60% for multi-surface releases.
2) Provide a single source of truth for launch timing across Console, Runtime, and API teams.
3) Enable automated safeholds that maintain customer-facing availability while avoiding manual rollback.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for existing SLA escalation or incident overrides.
- Not intended to manage long-lived capacity contracts (that's Dedicated planning).

Deliverables:
- PRD and sequencing rules (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/FLST+and+Cutover+Fuse+PRD
- API contract spec for signal input/output (JSON schema) and sample translator mappings.
- Console UX microflow for showing harmonized windows and safehold reasons.
- Runtime integration adapter (small shim) for Cutover Fuse that can trigger fallback policies via existing router API.
- Canary test harness and runbook for multi-region rollouts.

Acceptance criteria:
- FLST can ingest launch signals from 3 teams (runtime, console, dedicated) and produce unified window with conflict resolution rules documented.
- Cutover Fuse can enact a pause/throttle on the sequencer and route traffic to fallback variant within the configured SLO of 99.5% for a 30-minute window.
- Documentation, dashboards, and an on-call playbook are published and reviewed by Runtime and Console leads.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Overly aggressive automatic safeholds causing unnecessary delays. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, manual override flag, and canary boolean to prevent automatic fuse in early rollouts.
- Risk: Mismatch in signal semantics across teams. Mitigation: canonical schema and weekly alignment sync during cycle.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Sofia Martinez (owner)
- Eng leads: Marco Chen (runtime integration), Priya Rao (console), David Kim (dedicated)
- Design: Lina Ortega (console microflow)
- SRE/Oncall: Tanya Brooks

Rollout plan:
1) Jan week 3 - Design/PRD + schema draft.
2) Jan week 4 - Internal API review and small PoC: FLST ingest + basic conflict resolver.
3) Feb week 2 - Runtime shim + Cutover Fuse prototype that supports throttle/pause.
4) Feb week 3 - Canary with non-critical model rollout to EU region; monitor cost/latency dashboards.
5) Feb week 4 - Expand to cross-region doorbell test and publish runbook.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- Launch harmonization dashboard (Console): overlap rate, conflicts resolved, manual overrides.
- Cutover Fuse metrics (Runtime): fuse triggers, reason codes, average hold duration, downstream error rate.
- Canaries: latency and token-cost delta vs baseline (Grafana links below).

Artifacts & links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/FLST+and+Cutover+Fuse+PRD
- API schema (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1FLST-schema
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-signal-translator/pulls (see PR #48 for PoC)
- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/launch/launch-harmonization
- Runbook (PagerDuty + Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/FLST+Runbook

Open questions:
- Do we permit automated fuse triggers for Dedicated customer lanes by default, or require manual ops approval? (tentative: require ops approval for customer lanes)
- What is the canonical priority order for conflicting windows across Console, Runtime, and Sales (customer-driven launches)?

- Lina to deliver console microflow mockups by 2025-01-24.
- Schedule alignment meeting with Dedicated leads (David Kim) and SRE (Tanya Brooks) for 2025-01-21.
